solverCandidate.name: SPlisHSPlasH DFSPH (offline only)
solverCandidate.evidenceInspected: README: DFSPH support, partio/vtk export, MIT library license; dependencies have separate licenses
solverCandidate.execution: NOT RUN; no dependency on Blender; this contract is not a solver-native scene file

singleInitialBake.staticGeometry: horizontal plane and vertical finite paddle, dimensions recorded in scene export
singleInitialBake.initialState: relaxed coherent sphere; export actual particle masses and inventory rather than inferring mass from a mesh
singleInitialBake.refinement: halve fixed timestep and compare two particle spacings with identical physical volume and inputs; retain raw trajectories

runtimeContract.bulk: GPU interpolation of validated baked positions/velocities and thickness field; no live pressure solve
runtimeContract.secondarySpray: derive from resolved thinning/ejection in baked motion; inherit local velocity; debit mass from the same bulk identifiers exactly once
runtimeContract.deposit: landing transfers particle mass into connected world-keyed terrain wetness/height tiles; deposits follow sampled terrain; no decorative volume added
runtimeContract.optics: existing liquid rendering with measured thickness, dye absorption, Fresnel and HDR; not part of this commit
runtimeContract.bounds: one event first; fixed frame/particle/tile budgets; no synchronous per-frame GPU readback; no velocity/time scaling without renewed validation
runtimeContract.drying: explicit evaporation sink; retain residue separately; no abrupt unaccounted disappearance

gates.mass: bulk + spray + deposits + explicit sinks = initial mass; relative accounting error <= 1e-4
gates.energy: no unexplained gain exceeding 1% of initial available mechanical energy plus signed supplied boundary work; refinement must reduce error; report constraint dissipation separately
gates.surface: validate mesh enclosed volume independently of particle mass, including thin sheets; existing 16.6% error is not accepted automatically
gates.visual: close-range sequence must show coherent falling/spreading liquid before multiplying events; compare with water-balloon high-speed references
gates.performance: measure RTX CPU/GPU timing and frame tails on one event; no speedup claim from software GPU or operation counts
gates.stop: failed accounting, nonconvergent motion, inaccessible solver or implausible primary liquid blocks runtime integration; preserve existing balloon effects
